Chapter 8: The Surprising Power of Surrender
There’s a kind of freedom that shows up only when you finally stop trying to control every little thing.
For years, surrender almost felt like a sign of weakness to me—like it was something you did when you just couldn’t handle life on your own.
But as time went on, I started to realize: surrender isn’t about giving up. It’s about letting go of that exhausting illusion that you’re in charge of everything.
Life, as you know, has this funny way of reminding us just how little we can actually predict or manage.
Maybe you’ve seen it too—plans unraveling, relationships shifting, the future staying stubbornly out of focus.
Let me tell you about one woman’s turning point, during a season when everything felt up in the air. She’d been counting on a new job, and just like that, it vanished.
Suddenly, she was left anxious, untethered. The old urge to fix things, to force a solution, kicked in hard.
But this time... something was different.
Instead of scrambling for answers, she just sat quietly—hands open in her lap.
She remembered words from an old prayer: “Not my will, but yours.”
It wasn’t some dramatic, movie-worthy moment. There were no lightning bolts, no big revelations.
Just a gentle sense of release—a willingness to trust that she didn’t have to have everything figured out.
Most of us resist surrender because it feels a lot like losing, doesn’t it?
But in that quiet moment, it became clear: surrender was actually an act of trust—a way of admitting we’re not alone in all this.
The anxiety that had been gripping her started to loosen. In its place was a surprising sense of peace.
Over the next few weeks, new opportunities showed up.
Not the ones she would’ve chosen for herself, but, looking back, exactly what she needed.
It became obvious: letting go actually made room for something better.
Surrender doesn’t mean giving up or checking out.
It’s about showing up, doing what you can, and then letting the rest fall into hands far more capable than your own.
So if you’ve ever felt worn out from trying to control it all, here’s a gentle reminder: sometimes, your greatest strength is found in letting go.
